within_period_aggregates.name: early_day_hour_mean_count
within_period_aggregates.rationale: Leakage-safe substitute for lags: compute mean count for hours in days 1-13 of each month/year/workingday group. Available for both train validation rows (days 14-19) and test rows (days 20+) since they only use earlier-day training data.

within_period_aggregates.name: early_day_hour_median_count
within_period_aggregates.rationale: Median version of early-day aggregate to reduce outlier sensitivity.

within_period_aggregates.name: early_day_hour_std_count
within_period_aggregates.rationale: Within-period variability signal for the hour; experimental to validate utility against ablation gate.

sub_target_modeling.rationale: registered (corr=0.971) and casual (corr=0.690) are train-only additive components of count. Modeling each as a separate target and summing is the primary accuracy lever identified by the influence file. Each sub-model uses the same feature set (excluding casual/registered). Sub-model predictions summed to form count; both sub-models and the direct count model are candidates — best or blend selected by ensemble-meta.

feature_plan.rationale: Comprehensive: all 9 shared covariates used; datetime fully unpacked to hour/cyclic/ordinal features (top influence group); hour x season/workingday/weather interactions cover top-5 influence signals; per-fold target aggregates by hour/season/workingday capture temporal patterns leakage-free; within-period early-day aggregates are the safe lag substitute for this split structure; sub-target modeling (registered+casual) is the primary accuracy lever. Overfit guards: no lags (unsafe per influence file), experimental within-period aggregates flagged for ablation gate, all aggregates fit per fold only.

completeness_constraints.submission_frame_expansion: 6493 prediction rows in data/test/test.csv map directly to 6493 rows in sampleSubmission.csv (same datetime keys, one-to-one); no cross-join expansion needed — each datetime in test file is unique and corresponds to one submission row.
completeness_constraints.notes: No missingness in any column (all rates 0.0 per data_profile.json). RMSLE metric requires non-negative predictions; clip to 0 before expm1 inverse transform. Sub-target predictions (registered + casual) must each be clipped to >= 0 and summed; the sum is the count prediction.
